t: None of the funds in this Act shall be available to implement or enforce regulations that would result in the withdrawal of a slot from an air carrier at O’Hare International Airport under section 93.223 of title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations in excess of the total slots withdrawn from that air carrier as of October 31, 1993 if such additional slot is to be allocated to an air carrier or foreign air carrier under section 93.217 of title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the mention of "regulations" signals rulemaking, which would count as participation. But this is an appropriations limitation that bars the use of funds to enforce existing CFR provisions; it does not authorize or require new rulemaking, a comment period, a hearing, or consultation with any outside party. Air carriers are only the subject of the restriction and are given no role in a federal decision or any right to sue.
fable.s: None of the funds in this Act shall be available to implement or enforce regulations that would result in the withdrawal of a slot from an air carrier at O’Hare International Airport

qwen_block.w: This section is a funding restriction that limits the federal government's ability to enforce specific regulations regarding airport slot allocations. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties (such as airlines, states, or the public) before a decision is made. It merely restricts the use of funds for enforcement actions.
qwen_block.s: None of the funds in this Act shall be available to implement or enforce regulations that would result in the withdrawal of a slot from an air carrier at O’Hare International Airport under section 93.223 of title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations in excess of the total slots withdrawn from that air carrier as of October 31, 1993 if such additional slot is to be allocated to an air carrier or foreign air carrier under section 93.217 of title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations.

opus.w: This is an appropriations limit that stops funds from being used to enforce existing slot-withdrawal regulations. It does not authorize or require rulemaking, and it sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period or right to sue. The mention of 'regulations' might suggest a rulemaking grant like Example 6, but here the regulations already exist and the section only restricts enforcing them. The air carriers are affected parties, not participants in a federal decision.
opus.s: None of the funds in this Act shall be available to implement or enforce regulations that would result in the withdrawal of a slot from an air carrier at O’Hare International Airport
opus.b:
**Step 1.** The tempting reading is "Yes," because the section mentions federal regulations, and Example 6 counts a grant of rulemaking authority as participation. That reading fails here. This section is a funding limit: it blocks money from being used to implement or enforce existing slot-withdrawal rules (14 CFR 93.223 and 93.217). It does not authorize or require any new rulemaking. It also creates no comment period, hearing, consultation, advisory body or right to sue. Air carriers appear only as the parties whose slots are affected, not as participants in any decision.

**Step 2.**

qwen_chat.w: This section imposes a funding restriction on the implementation of specific regulations regarding airport slot allocations. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or airlines) in the decision-making process. The reference to air carriers is regarding the subject of the regulation, not their involvement in the regulatory decision.
qwen_chat.s: None of the funds in this Act shall be available to implement or enforce regulations that would result in the withdrawal of a slot from an air carrier at O’Hare International Airport under section 93.223 of title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations in excess of the total slots withdrawn from that air carrier as of October 31, 1993 if such additional slot is to be allocated to an air carrier or foreign air carrier under section 93.217 of title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the allocation of slots to air carriers involves public participation because it affects private companies. However, the text itself does not mandate any consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory process involving outside parties. It simply sets a limit on how many slots can be withdrawn and reallocated. The decision-making process described is purely internal to the regulatory framework (referencing CFR sections) and does not require interaction with entities outside the federal government.
